disagreements.topic: Re-entry Modal Membrane Presentation vs Finite Support Preservation
disagreements.observation: Candidate X implements an explicit dialog (#loomReentryModal) after Continuation 1 reaches REST.
disagreements.primary_claim: The modal creates conversational rupture, increases route burden on mobile, and presents an unbriefed cognitive choice to the operator before they know what the AI response entails.
disagreements.counter_claim: The modal boundary is mathematically necessary to prevent quotient collapse between ordinary chat (A=0) and governed continuation (A=1) across turn transitions.
disagreements.falsifier: Mobile UX trial showing user confusion, dialog dismissal, or route abandonment vs automated test showing zero illegal file carriage.
disagreements.missing_witness: Human-facing mobile browser trial comparing modal presentation against inline non-modal boundary affordances.

disagreements.topic: Automated Headless Test Execution vs Behavioral Observability
disagreements.observation: GitHub Actions Linux runner executed 13/13 Candidate X tests using JSDOM with exit code 0.
disagreements.primary_claim: The relational invariants (predecessor binding, single-turn arming, REST boundary) survived exogenous transfer to an independent execution host.
disagreements.counter_claim: JSDOM is an incomplete observation sensor; it lacks rendering, layout bounding, and touch event geometry. Replay stability under perturbation remains unmeasured and HELD.
disagreements.falsifier: A real mobile browser run where modal styling renders occluded or unclickable despite JSDOM asserting DOM existence.
disagreements.missing_witness: Real multi-browser cross-platform headed/headless witness with viewport layout validation.

disagreements.topic: Historical R4 Episode Status vs Post-Merge Runtime Capability
disagreements.observation: Historical episode R4 proved route closure for 1 continuation at t1; post-merge audit discovered runtime permitted Continuation 2 at t2.
disagreements.primary_claim: R4 remains an immutable historical episode. Discovering runtime capability at t2 amends the product capability model but cannot rewrite the R4 empirical record.
disagreements.counter_claim: Presenting R4 as proving 'Model A terminality' misleads operators if the executable code actually permitted further turns.
disagreements.falsifier: Audit log proving whether the R4 observer physically stopped vs whether the server refused a second continuation.
disagreements.missing_witness: Replay audit of R4 network traces distinguishing client cessation from server rejection.
